clue.text: Carol and Lily mended in confusion, which is how we clued the other Across clues

definitions.text: which is how we clued the other Across clues

parts.note: to carol is to sing, the verb taken as the plain word

indicators.note: the words Lily and mended are thrown into confusion, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women, Carol and Lily, patch something up in a muddle, and the setters admit this is how they wrote the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on 'single': in every other Across clue the wordplay gives each doubled letter of the answer only once, and the grid entry repeats it.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-mindedly normally means with one purpose; here it jokes that the clues were minded to give doubled letters singly.

clue.text: One taking major steps gutted significant additional clause

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
a rider is a clause added to a bill or contract

explanation.surface: Someone making big moves, after an important extra clause has been stripped out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strider walks with long steps, so it is someone taking big strides.

clue.text: The greatest group of nine almost adopting earth tone

indicators.note: the shortened group takes in the colour, holding it inside
almost means not quite all, so the group's last letter is removed

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine performers
umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: The best of a nine-piece band, nearly, takes on a muddy brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is the top of the rankings, the best of all.

clue.text: Relaxed call?

parts.note: the surface reading: easygoing, unhurried
the question mark asks for a call that is relaxed, read as a description of a manner of speaking

explanation.walkthrough: A short cryptic definition: what kind of call is relaxed? One made in a casual, unbothered way.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back is an informal word for relaxed and easygoing, so a calm, casual call fits it.

clue.text: Mounting a precious stone that's huge

indicators.note: in a Down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a gem

explanation.surface: Setting a jewel in a ring, a stone that is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal for enormous, from the prefix meaning million or great.

clue.text: City in the South: Salerno?

parts.note: the surface reading: a quiz question about a southern city
the setter's reading: Salerno is a fresh arrangement of the letters of the French city Orleans, so it is a renewed version of it

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: Salerno is a rearrangement of ORLEANS, so Salerno could be called a new Orleans. The question mark flags the wordplay hiding in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is the largest city in Louisiana, in the American South.

clue.text: Lombardi, after end of game show

indicators.note: Lombardi's first name is placed after that final letter
end of picks out the final letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written; only its final letter is used
Vince Lombardi, the American football coach

explanation.surface: Vince Lombardi appears on a programme once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Lombardi was the famed coach of the Green Bay Packers; the Super Bowl trophy bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to reveal or display a feeling or quality, so it means to show.

clue.text: Free time put into building toy

indicators.note: the time letter is placed inside the toy brand

parts.note: Lego, the plastic brick toy

explanation.surface: Spare time gets spent on playing with plastic bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free time' reads as leisure, but Free is the definition and time is just T.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go is to release someone or something from your grip, which is to free it.

clue.text: Kind of angel I mistreated

indicators.note: the letters of angel and I are handled roughly and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession that some type of angel was badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of angel' reads as a sort of angel, but Kind is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means friendly and pleasant in manner, a close synonym of kind.

clue.text: Circle around in the morning, crashing into…

indicators.note: the circle's letters go around the morning abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a ring is a circle
AM, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Someone loops around early in the day and drives into something, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the theme in 1-Across, the wordplay supplies only one M of the doubled pair; the grid needs both.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramming is driving forcefully into something, so it is a direct synonym phrase for colliding with it.

clue.text: …line in colorless trim

indicators.note: the line's letter goes in the middle of the colourless word

parts.note: white is often called the absence of colour
L

explanation.surface: A line appears in some plain, undyed trimming, continuing the previous clue's sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme again: the wordplay gives one T, and the grid entry doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To whittle is to pare away by shaving small pieces, so it means to trim something down.

clue.text: Down with networks and nerds

parts.note: D, the abbreviation for down in crossword grids
webs are networks

explanation.surface: A protest slogan against computer networks and the geeks who run them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down with' reads as a protest cry, but Down is just D joined with the networks; the theme means the wordplay gives only one E.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a socially awkward, studious person, a close synonym of nerd.

clue.text: Sib replacing bacterium's energy in vegetable

indicators.note: the sibling takes the place of the energy letter, so one letter is swapped for another piece

parts.note: E. coli is the familiar gut bacterium
a sib is a sibling, here a bro

explanation.surface: A lab note about a related strain displacing a bacterium's energy source inside a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy' is E, the first letter of E. coli; the theme means the wordplay gives only one C.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green plant whose flower heads are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: A collection of stars or athletes from Detroit, shifting 50 into a wager

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the 50 moves out of the team's name to somewhere else

parts.note: the Detroit Lions, an American football team

indicators.note: the moved letter lands inside the wager

parts.note: a bet
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Choose between a constellation and a Detroit sports team while moving fifty dollars into a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' and 'athletes' both suggest sports celebrities, but the stars are real ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion's Belt is the row of three bright stars across the middle of the constellation Orion, an asterism.

clue.text: Retro poet's contraction, made better, arose again

indicators.note: retro means looking back, so the poet's word is read backwards

parts.note: o'er, the poetic shortening of over
cured, healed

explanation.surface: A poet's old-fashioned shortened word, once improved, came back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme halves both doubled letters: the wordplay gives REO plus CURED, one C and one R.
explanation.definitionFit: Reoccurred means happened or came up again, a fair synonym for arose again.

clue.text: Dog returning what I threw?

indicators.note: the dog comes back, so its name runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador retriever

explanation.surface: A retriever brings back the thing its owner has thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a ball is one thing I might throw. The theme gives only one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is the typical object thrown for a dog to fetch, so it is an example.

clue.text: Fishing bait is lame, wrong, messed-up

indicators.note: the letters of lame and wrong are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that some bait is useless, mistaken and in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' looks like a second anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'messed-up' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An angleworm is an earthworm used by anglers on a hook, so it is a bait.

clue.text: Baseball Hall of Famer traveled west, taking an automobile

indicators.note: the travel word takes the car inside it

parts.note: rode
a car

explanation.surface: A baseball great drove west in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Carew was a Minnesota Twins and California Angels hitter inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Carew is an enshrined member of baseball's Hall of Fame, so he is an example.

clue.text: Nourish government agent

wordplay.note: a fed is an American federal agent

explanation.surface: Instruction to give food to a federal officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme means the wordplay gives only one E of the doubled pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed is to give food, which is what nourishing means.

clue.text: Search for maturity

parts.note: taken as written
age, the state of being old enough

explanation.surface: Looking for the moment of growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Search for' reads as one phrase, but for is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to hunt around for food or supplies, so it means to search.

clue.text: Spy on (stare at) wasteful endeavor

parts.note: James Bond, the fictional spy
to ogle is to stare at lecherously

explanation.surface: Keeping watch on a target turns out to be pointless work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the spy on top of the staring word; the theme drops one O and one G from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A boondoggle is American slang for a pointless project that wastes time or public money.

clue.text: Photography pioneer adjusted a steam nozzle's opening

indicators.note: the letters are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written; only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with the mouth of a steam nozzle on an early camera.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eastman founded Kodak and popularised roll film.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eastman founded Kodak and brought roll film and cheap cameras to the public, a founder of modern photography.

clue.text: Zigzag look in pan

indicators.note: the look word sits in the middle of the criticism word

parts.note: to pan a show is to slam it
lo, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A wavy pattern seen when peering into a cooking pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like a cooking pot, but it means harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a race weaving between gates, a zigzag course.

clue.text: Steals cattle with no evidence of neglect

wordplay.note: to rustle is to steal livestock

explanation.surface: A cattle thief at work, claimed to leave no sign of having slacked off.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme leaves one S off the wordplay. Rust is the usual mark of metal left uncared for, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustless means free of rust, and rust is the tell-tale sign that metal has been left uncared for.

clue.text: Colossal volley contents!

indicators.note: the answer is the contents of the two words, sitting inside them

parts.note: taken as written; the answer runs across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the size of what a barrage holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the answer sits inside 'Colossal volley', and a colossal volley is what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a volley of fire.

clue.text: Reach those with expertise

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with people who know their stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme gives one C and one S in the wordplay; the grid doubles both.
explanation.definitionFit: To access a place or a person is to get to them, a synonym of reach.

clue.text: We hear second son is competent

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken, so it sounds like the answer

parts.note: Abel, the second son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: Word reaches us that the family's younger boy is capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means having the skill or power to do something, a synonym of competent.

clue.text: Storm engulfs Long Island, where Jesus once walked

indicators.note: the storm swallows the island abbreviation, surrounding it

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
LI, the usual abbreviation for the New York island

explanation.surface: A storm sweeps over an island, recalling the Biblical calming of the waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme gives only one E from the wordplay. Jesus is said to have walked on the Sea of Galilee.
explanation.definitionFit: The region and lake in northern Israel are where the Gospels place Jesus walking on water.

clue.text: Rambo getting drunk in a saloon

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the action hero's name is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The action hero gets plastered at a Wild West bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme means the five letters of Rambo give one R and one O; the grid entry doubles them.
explanation.definitionFit: A barroom is a room with a bar serving drinks, which is what an American saloon is.

clue.text: Farm animal swallowing bug — a sign for some female politicians

indicators.note: the farm animal takes the bug inside it, enclosing it

parts.note: a cow
a mite is a tiny bug
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A cow gulping an insect is taken as a portent by women in office.
explanation.walkthrough: Three letters are doubled in the grid, M, T and E; per the theme the wordplay gives each once.
explanation.definitionFit: Committeewomen are women serving on a political party committee, so they are a kind of female politician.
